Another manufacturer, whose average fuel economy is confortably above the AFES and whose fleet includes nonpassenger automobiles of 6,000 pounds and less GVWR similar to the first manufacturer's less fuel economical ones, may attempt to increase his share of that portion of the nonpassenger automobile market by increasing his production of his similar nonpassenger automobiles. By limiting the proposal to a 1-year standard, the agency will have additional opportunity to explore further the likelihood and magnitude of this type of shift before proposing AFES's for subsequent model years.

Another reason that the agency is promulgating an AFES for a single MY is that the agency has tentatively determined to set the AFES for MY 1979 near the level of average fuel economy which the manufacturers are planning to achieve in that MY. The reason for taking this approach is the agency's uncertainty about the sensitivity of the market to changes in nonpassenger automobiles of 6,000 pounds and less GVWR and about the likelihood of such sensitivity resulting in the shifts discsussed above.
